crime: Every evening, one of the prisoners walked the long path around the lake to draw the mansion's lights from the far shore. And every evening, {WITCH_NAME} used her Magic to run straight across the water, her feet never sinking, to sit beside her.
One evening at seven, by the lake, the girl handed her the sketchbook full of those lights. "You keep it. I've drawn it enough."
{WITCH_NAME}'s mother had given away her things one by one, her coat to a neighbour, her books to her daughter, and then one morning she was gone. People hand out what they own before they go.

There by the lake, she strangled the girl with her scarf until she was still. Then she picked her up and ran across the lake with her, and sat her down in her spot on the far shore, facing the mansion's lights, where she always drew.

At ten past seven, {WITCH_NAME} came back into the lounge and stayed among the prisoners all evening. They had watched the girl leave the lounge at five to seven for the long lake path, twenty minutes on foot to her spot. So in the trial court, the prisoners ruled that she had walked there and been strangled where she sat, by which time {WITCH_NAME} was already back among them.

Then one prisoner turned over the dead girl's shoes. The soles were clean, without a single one of the pine needles the lake path leaves on everyone who walks it. The prisoners understood: she had never walked the path. {WITCH_NAME} had carried her across the water before ten past seven.
fields.epitaph: It was only a sketchbook. She outran a goodbye that was never coming.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Runs Ahead of Every Goodbye
execution: The execution stand raises a deep, round iron pool with sheer walls. She stands on an iron plinth in the middle of the water. On the rim above her stands an iron mother.
The iron mother lowers an iron coat onto her shoulders. "You keep it."
The plinth sinks from under her, and she runs out onto the water. It holds her up only while she keeps moving.
The iron mother walks away around the rim without looking back. She runs after her across the water and never gains.
At last she stumbles to a stop under the coat. The water gives way, and the coat drags her under. The water over her goes still, while the iron mother walks on around the rim.

magic.name: Water Strider
magic.text: She can run across water, thin ice or a taut rope as if it were solid ground.
